To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the fasting fibrinogen synthetic rates are increased in weight-losing pancreatic and gastric cancer patients compared with healthy controls and that feeding increases the fibrinogen synthetic response in cancer patients but not in healthy controls.
in the fasting state fibrinogen synthesis was increased in weight-losing patients with pancreatic cancer, and this increase was further augmented after a feeding meal.
in weight-losing pancreatic patients, albumin and fibrinogen synthesis rates are upregulated after a meal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of cachexia in cancer patients.
the mechanisms of protein metabolism in the cancer patient and has demonstrated the importance of the acute-phase response and the effect of the oral feeding of protein on protein metabolism.
the synthesis of plasma proteins in the liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the acute-phase response is a feature of cancer cachexia and that this response is exaggerated in the presence of weight loss and is further enhanced by oral meal feeding.
the acute-phase protein response in cancer patients is similar to that in healthy individuals but is exaggerated by feeding in the cachectic state.
in the fasting state albumin synthesis is not impaired but that fibrinogen synthesis rate is increased in weight-losing pancreatic and other cancer patients, and both are upregulated on feeding.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the fed state in cancer patients, fibrinogen production is increased, and this may contribute to the hyperfibrinogenemia seen in this group of patients.
the liver is not in a "starvation" state, but rather a "fed" or even an "acute-phase response" state in cachectic patients.
the synthesis of acute phase proteins is increased in weight-losing pancreatic patients, but the synthesis of the negative acute-phase proteins albumin and transthyretin is not.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in cancer patients, the synthesis of fibrinogen is upregulated in the fasted state, whereas albumins synthesis is not.
, in cancer patients with weight loss, fibrinogen is synthesized in increased amounts.
the liver is not in a state of failure in cancer cachexia.
